state: code-seam@v2: THINKME -> [TICKETME] -> BUILDME -> PROVEME -> WATCHME(reflection_earns_its_ask) -> PROVED
intention: The apprentice learns that the test it was driven against failed, and gets a bounded number of further attempts inside the same conversation.
why: THE APPRENTICE CANNOT LEARN THAT ITS TEST FAILED, AND THE FIELD THAT WOULD SHOW IT READS EXACTLY LIKE SUCCESS. driver.py:279 pins auto_test=False with the comment 'WE run the test, so its result is ours to carry'. aider reflects on self.reflected_message, and the only thing that sets it from a test is `if edited and self.auto_test` at base_coder.py:1616-1622 — so with auto_test off, the driver runs the test AFTER coder.run() returns and nothing ever reaches the model. Measured 2026-08-17: a drive passed max_reflections=1 and recorded num_reflections=0, which reads as convergence and is the opposite — nothing could reach it. A severed feedback loop and a converged one are the same number, which is why this is a defect rather than a missing feature.
how: Compose aider's own reflection loop rather than build a second one beside it. base_coder.run_one already loops `while message:` on self.reflected_message and stops at max_reflections (base_coder.py:932-944); the only thing that sets reflected_message from a test is `if edited and self.auto_test` at base_coder.py:1616-1622, and the driver pins auto_test=False. So: carry the brief's test_cmd as a STRING in the venv payload and construct the Coder with auto_test=True and that test_cmd, leaving the parent's own run_test exactly where it is as the record's authority. Measured constraint that decides the shape (CairnCommons/notes/aiders-own-reflection-loop-is-reachable-and-a-callable-test-cmd-is-not.json): a CALLABLE test_cmd — which would have kept 'WE run the test' literally true — raises TypeError on every system-prompt format, because test_cmd is also concatenated into the prompt unguarded at base_coder.py:1169.
traces_to: Telos 5 — build something that is self-improving. An apprentice that reads its own failing test and tries again is that aim at its smallest honest scale; today the loop is severed and the field that would show it (num_reflections) reads 0 for the opposite reason. Secondarily Law 3: `num_reflections: 0` is currently an unmeasured claim of convergence dressed as a measurement.
gates: PROVE GATE (class invariant): the tester runs the node's proof and emits a validation, verdict and seal from the same hand — cairn/devices/aider_shim/proofs/test_driver.py (30 teeth today) grows the teeth for this seam, sealed via TesterDevice().run_proof(..., isolation='netns'). The teeth a hollow build could not pass: the payload carries test_cmd and auto_test and the Coder is constructed with them (asserted through the real _DRIVE arrangement, not a mock of it), a drive whose test fails records num_reflections >= 1, and a drive with max_reflections=0 still records 0 — the cap must remain the thing that stops it. FEEDS-BACK-TO-ORIGIN-ON-FAILURE (class invariant): a red proof kicks back to build at the point of creation (CP2). EXTRA GATE — durability: committed and pushed, on the emit chokepoint. EMISSION GATE: the WATCHME crossing refuses unless cairn/devices/aider_shim/probes/reflection_earns_its_ask.py declares a module-level frozen PROBE carrying both a carry and an enough.
falsifier: A drive whose first attempt fails the test records num_reflections >= 1 and at least two asks in the fence's log, with the second ask's payload containing the test's failure text. Wrong-intent horizon: if reflected drives do not raise the applied-and-passing rate above the unreflected baseline over the next 5 driven pieces, the loop is cost without learning and the finding is that the ceiling was the brief, not the feedback.
horizon: Five driven pieces. If reflected drives do not raise the applied-and-passing rate above the unreflected baseline drawn from the same drives.jsonl, the loop is cost without learning and the finding is that the apprentice's ceiling was the BRIEF, not the feedback.
children: none, because the seam is bounded to one file and one already-existing proof: the change is a payload field plus two constructor arguments in cairn/devices/aider_shim/driver.py, and its teeth grow in cairn/devices/aider_shim/proofs/test_driver.py. The probe named in the watch is not a child — it is this node's own WATCHME obligation, armed before the crossing at the berth the spec names.

watchme.trigger: every drive recorded to ~/.cairn/devices/aider_shim/0/drives.jsonl — the driver's own record write is the event that already fires, and nothing polls. The probe reads the row's num_reflections against its asks and its test outcome, so a drive that never reflected is a data point too rather than a gap.
watchme.enough: when five drives carrying num_reflections >= 1 have been recorded AND their applied-and-passing rate has a consistent relationship to the unreflected baseline drawn from the same file. Stop early and loudly on either falsifying observation: a reflected drive that ends WORSE than its first attempt left it — the applied-and-self-cancelling state the edit-survival probe's vocabulary has no word for, and the one this loop could actively manufacture by giving a copying apprentice more turns to copy; or a drive whose second ask does not carry the test's failure text, which means the mechanism reports firing while feeding the apprentice nothing.
watchme.carrier: a verdict artifact against THIS ticket's falsifier: per drive, num_reflections, the ask count and each ask's prompt_eval_count (a reflected ask that is a cache hit is not a second opinion), whether the second ask's payload contains the test's failure text, the test outcome of the drive as recorded, and the survival disposition of the files it touched
watchme.nexus: the hypothesize tree — the same one aider_shim_offload_yield and aider_shim_edit_survival deposit to, deliberately, so the three watches answer their different questions over ONE drives.jsonl population rather than each demanding its own five real tickets
watchme.consumer: Akien at triage, for whom this is the offload-more vs pull-back decision and specifically the cost half of it — reflection multiplies asks against a metered host, so 'it helps' and 'it helps enough' are different answers and only he settles the second; and CC, who is the party that would otherwise read num_reflections as convergence, which is the exact misreading that bore this ticket

distinctions_recorded: AFTER THIS CHANGE THE TEST RUNS TWICE ON A DRIVE THAT REACHES AN EDIT, and only one of them is evidence: aider's, inside the loop, is the apprentice's feedback signal; the parent's run_test is the record's authority and is what DriveResult.test carries. A reader finding two invocations and assuming redundancy would delete the wrong one. This distinction belongs in the code at the seam, not only here.

THE DRIVER'S EXISTING COMMENT IS NOT CONTRADICTED. 'WE run the test, so its result is ours to carry' protects whose result the RECORD carries — it exists so DriveResult.test is not scraped out of aider's chat. It does not protect aider's ignorance of the test; that was a consequence of the setting rather than its purpose, and the record's authority never moves.

A CALLABLE test_cmd IS THE DESIGN THAT WOULD HAVE KEPT THE COMMENT LITERALLY TRUE AND IT IS IMPOSSIBLE. commands.cmd_test accepts one (commands.py:1002-1010), but test_cmd is also concatenated into the system prompt unguarded at base_coder.py:1169, so a callable raises `TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for +: 'function' and 'str'` on every message format. Measured in the shim's own venv, both variants, before this cast. Recorded so the next reader does not re-derive it from the call site, where the two designs look equally available.

THE PARENT CANNOT OWN THE LOOP WITHOUT DISCARDING THE CONVERSATION. run_in_venv is a one-shot subprocess and a Coder does not survive the process boundary, so a parent-side retry would re-pay full context and lose the model's own reasoning between attempts — the expensive shape AND the one least likely to converge.
